title: Night to rest, day to earn, both out of mercy.
subtitle: The rhythm of a day as a reason to give thanks

row.title: make it up
sub: in the night, or the day

then: After the two questions about endless night and endless day, Allah says both were made {reward}out of His mercy{/reward}: rest at night, travel and work by day. Ibn Kathir adds that {idea}whoever misses something at night can make it up during the day{/idea}, and the reverse.
now: You slept through Fajr, or the workday ate your plans for Quran. It feels like the day is lost. {idea}The night and day take turns so you can catch up.{/idea} The rhythm itself is a second chance.
old: If I miss a good deed at its time, the chance is gone.
new: Allah made night and day follow each other so I can make up what I missed and thank Him.
try: Make up one missed good habit from earlier today before you sleep tonight.

title: The same question again: where are they now?
subtitle: Asked before every witness on the Day
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}another call by way of rebuke{/trap} for those who worshipped others besides Allah, made {idea}before all the witnesses{/idea}. The question from verse 62 returns, right after the verses about night and day: who else gave you those?
now: You just read that Allah alone brings morning and night. Now the question returns. {idea}Hearing it twice is a gift{/idea}: a second chance to check what you lean on, today, before it is asked for real.
old: I already heard this warning, so it is not for me.
new: Allah repeats the question so I keep checking whom I truly rely on.
try: Before bed, ask yourself honestly: what did I rely on most today, other than Allah?

title: Bring your proof. And every invented claim disappears.
subtitle: A witness from every nation
then: Mujahid said the witness from every nation means {idea}a Messenger{/idea}. Then they are asked for proof of their claim that Allah had partners. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they will not speak and will not find any answer{/trap}; the lies they invented will vanish.
now: You have explanations ready for the things you know are wrong: stress, everyone does it, it is complicated. {idea}Picture saying them in front of Allah.{/idea} If they fade even in your imagination, let them go now.
old: I can always explain my choices if asked.
new: Before Allah only the truth stands, and invented excuses vanish.
try: Pick one excuse you use often and drop it for a day. Do the thing or admit why you do not.

title: So rich his keys were heavy, so proud he oppressed.
subtitle: Qarun, and the advice he was given
then: Ibn Abbas and others said Qarun was {idea}Musa's paternal cousin{/idea}. He was given treasures whose keys a band of strong men could not carry, yet he {trap}behaved arrogantly toward his own people{/trap}. The righteous among them advised him sincerely: do not exult.
now: Your cousin buys a new car and the family chat fills with photos and hints. Or you got the bonus and you cannot stop mentioning it. {trap}Wealth can make you look down on your own people.{/trap} Notice the urge to show off.
old: If I have more, I have the right to show it off.
new: Allah does not love those who gloat, so wealth calls for humility, not display.
try: Next time you want to post or mention something you bought, pause and skip it.

title: Use it for the Hereafter, enjoy your share, be generous.
subtitle: The best financial advice ever given

row.title: do good
sub: as Allah did good to you

then: His people told Qarun to {idea}use his wealth to draw closer to his Lord{/idea}, and not forget his lawful share: food, drink, clothing, home, family. Ibn Kathir: your Lord, your self, your family and your visitors {reward}each have rights over you{/reward}. Be generous as Allah was generous to you.
now: Payday arrives. Rent, a meal out with your family, a transfer to your mother, something to the food bank. {idea}That is this verse in a banking app.{/idea} Not guilt about enjoying it, not forgetting where it came from.
old: Being religious means feeling guilty about enjoying money.
new: I can enjoy my lawful share while using what Allah gave me for the Hereafter and for others.
try: On your next payday, set aside one small amount for someone in need before anything else.

title: I earned this myself, he said.
subtitle: Mistaking a gift for proof you deserve it

row.title: Allah loves me
sub: or He would not give it

then: Qarun answered his advisers: {trap}"I was only given it because of knowledge I have."{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains the meaning as: Allah gave me this because He knows I deserve it. He notes this is what people of little knowledge say when they see someone wealthy. Many before him were {trap}stronger and richer{/trap}, and were destroyed.
now: You worked hard, studied, took the risk, and it paid off. It is tempting to think: I made this happen, and that is why I have it. {idea}The skill, the health, the timing were all given.{/idea}
old: I have what I have because I earned it and deserve it.
new: My success is Allah's gift and a test, not proof that I am better.
try: Name one thing you are proud of achieving. List three things Allah gave you that made it possible.

title: He paraded his wealth, and the crowd wished for it.
subtitle: Envy at the procession
then: Qarun went out before his people in all his splendor: {trap}fine clothes, fine horses, servants and retinue{/trap}. Those whose desires were for the world said {trap}"if only we had what Qarun has"{/trap}, calling him very lucky.
now: Holiday photos, a friend's new kitchen, an influencer's car. You scroll and feel smaller. {trap}Your own life starts to look poor.{/trap} That feeling is the crowd at Qarun's parade.
old: People with more than me are the lucky ones.
new: Envying someone's display shows where my own heart is pointed.
try: When envy hits while scrolling today, close the app and thank Allah for one thing you have.

title: Allah's reward is better, and only the patient reach it.
subtitle: What people of knowledge said at the parade

row.title: the patient
sub: who let go of the craving

then: People of beneficial knowledge answered the crowd: {reward}Allah's reward is better for those who believe and do good{/reward}. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that Allah has prepared what no eye has seen and no ear has heard. Ibn Jarir said it is reached by {idea}those who patiently give up love of this world{/idea}.
now: Your friend posts the new car; you post nothing, saving for your parents' care. It does not look like winning. {reward}What Allah has prepared is beyond what anyone can see.{/reward} Patience with your own life is the price.
old: If I cannot have it now, I am missing out.
new: Patiently not chasing this world is the way to a reward far better than any parade.
try: Tell one friend something kind about their life today instead of comparing it to yours.
